rationale: The hospital needs both what happens to referred patients and why referrals fail, to design a pathway. A convergent mixed methods design runs a quantitative strand (housing outcomes of referred patients from provider data; emergency use against eligible non-referred inpatients matched on prior service use with propensity weights and a negative control outcome, c4) alongside peer-led interviews with referred people and staff (c3, c5), integrated in a joint display that maps failure points to outcomes. The retrieved comparison (c1) and programme data (c2) show both strands are needed.
alternatives: Quantitative comparison only (refused: would not explain why referrals fail)
Qualitative study only (refused: the executive needs outcomes)
Explanatory sequential design (refused: the September 2027 deadline does not allow the strands to run one after the other)
whyNotMoreComplex: A randomised evaluation of the referral pathway would need a pathway to test; this study builds it.

decision.statement: Conduct a convergent mixed methods study of hospital referrals to housing first in 2024 and 2025, linking referred patients' tenancy outcomes to hospital use, comparing emergency use with matched eligible non-referred inpatients, and interviewing referred people and staff with a peer researcher.
decision.question: What study should inform the hospital's housing-first referral pathway?

criteria.text: Referral failure points and outcome differences are both plausible and measurable.
A fair comparison group can be defined for emergency use.
The provider refuses any sharing of tenancy outcomes.

gates.requirement: Research ethics approval of the protocol
gates.evidence: REB-2026-188 approved 2026-09-01 with the condition that tenancy data wait for a data-sharing agreement, supplied by the investigator

gates.requirement: Signed data-sharing agreement with the housing-first provider naming a data custodian
gates.evidence: The provider's board rejected the first proposal on 2026-08-19 because no data custodian was named, supplied by the investigator

alternatives: Quantitative comparison of hospital use only
decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1 to c4 from retrieved records; one gate met and one unmet, so the study is selected but cannot start until the agreement is signed.

summary: Convergent mixed methods study recommended; ethics gate met, data-sharing gate unmet.
